description: A six-panel composite (2x3) of transmission electron micrographs, lettered (a)-(f), comparing tempered martensite, retained austenite and ε-carbides in two steels; the caption assigns (a-c) to the 0Al steel and (d-f) to the 1.3Al steel. (a) and (d) are bright-field TEM images (both with 0.3 µm scale bars) of tempered martensitic laths; yellow arrows in (a) mark "Sharp lath boundaries", while (d) uses a yellow ellipse and arrow to mark "High density dislocation". (b) and (e) are dark-field TEM images (0.3 µm scale bars) in which thin bright films along lath boundaries are arrowed as "Retained austenite"; their upper-right SAED insets index austenite (γ) and martensite (M) reflections with printed zone axes Z=[111]M/Z=[110]γ (b) and Z=[100]M/Z=[100]γ (e). (c) and (f) are higher-magnification TEM images (100 nm scale bars) with yellow arrows pointing to needle-like "ε-carbide" precipitates; their SAED insets index hcp ε reflections, e.g. (002)ε/(111)ε with Z=[110]ε in (f). Collectively the panels show that both steels keep lath-shaped tempered martensite with sharp boundaries and high dislocation density, that thin retained-austenite films persist at lath boundaries, and that fine, commonly aligned needle-like ε-carbides precipitate inside the laths; no numeric axis values are printed, only scale bars and annotation text.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph of the 0Al steel after tempering, 0.3 µm scale bar; tempered martensitic laths with a high dislocation density and dark, mottled contrast. Yellow arrows label 'Sharp lath boundaries'.

Dark-field TEM micrograph, 0.3 µm scale bar; yellow arrows point to thin bright films along lath boundaries labelled 'Retained austenite'. Upper-right SAED inset shows austenite and martensite reflections, indexed (101)γ/(112)M/(011)M/(220)γ/(111)γ/(331)γ with Z=[111]M and Z=[110]γ.

Higher-magnification TEM micrograph, 100 nm scale bar; yellow arrows mark needle-like precipitates labelled 'ε-carbide'. Upper-right SAED inset indexes ε-carbide ((200)ε, (011)ε, (002)ε, (020)ε, (220)ε) and martensite spots with zone axes Z=[100]M and Z=[001]ε.
Bright-field TEM micrograph of the 1.3Al steel, 0.3 µm scale bar; a yellow ellipse and arrow highlight regions labelled 'High density dislocation' within the martensitic laths.

Dark-field TEM micrograph, 0.3 µm scale bar; yellow arrows indicate bright thin films labelled 'Retained austenite' along lath boundaries. Upper-right SAED inset indexes austenite (002)γ, (022)γ, (020)γ and martensite (111)M, (011)M, (020)M with Z=[100]M and Z=[100]γ.

Higher-magnification TEM micrograph, 100 nm scale bar; yellow arrows point to several long needle-like precipitates labelled 'ε-carbide', aligned along a common direction. Upper-right SAED inset shows (002)ε, (111)ε and (111)M reflections with Z=[110]ε.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a bright-field TEM micrograph of the 0Al steel with a 0.3 µm scale bar, in which yellow arrows mark 'Sharp lath boundaries' of tempered martensite.
Panel (d) is a bright-field TEM micrograph of the 1.3Al steel with a 0.3 µm scale bar, in which a yellow ellipse and arrow highlight regions labelled 'High density dislocation'.
Panels (b) and (e) are dark-field TEM images (0.3 µm scale bars) in which yellow arrows label thin bright films at lath boundaries as 'Retained austenite'.
The SAED inset in (b) contains reflections indexed (111)γ, (220)γ, (331)γ together with (011)M, (101)M and (112)M, with zone axes Z=[111]M and Z=[110]γ printed.
The SAED inset in (e) is indexed with austenite (002)γ, (022)γ, (020)γ and martensite (011)M, (111)M, (020)M, with zone axes Z=[100]M and Z=[100]γ printed.
Panels (c) and (f) are higher-magnification TEM images with 100 nm scale bars, in which yellow arrows point to long needle-like precipitates labelled 'ε-carbide' aligned along a common direction.
The SAED inset in (f) shows spots indexed (002)ε and (111)ε with Z=[110]ε next to a martensite (111)M spot.
The SAED inset in (c) indexes ε-carbide reflections (200)ε, (011)ε, (002)ε, (020)ε and (220)ε together with martensite reflections, with zone axes Z=[100]M and Z=[001]ε.
No numeric values or axis scales are printed on any micrograph; the only quantitative marks are the scale bars (0.3 µm in (a), (b), (d), (e) and 100 nm in (c), (f)) and the yellow annotation labels.
The caption states that panels (a-c) are the 0Al steel and (d-f) the 1.3Al steel, i.e. the two panels in each column pair the two steels.
The citing text states the needle-like ε-carbides are 100–500 nm long and 3–10 nm wide and precipitated uniformly within the laths along a common crystallographic direction.

The citing text states the retained austenite was indexed as (110)γ adjacent to martensite (111)M, consistent with the Kurdjumov-Sachs orientation relationship {111}γ//{110}M, <110>γ//<111>M; these Miller indices are not legible as such in the pixel data.

The citing text elsewhere gives the hcp ε-carbides as approximately 100–500 nm in length and 2–4 nm in thickness, which disagrees with the 3–10 nm width quoted in the same paper; no dimension is printed in this figure to arbitrate.
The citing text attributes to Fig. 3 the observation that the martensitic matrix retains sharp lath boundaries and well-defined structure after tempering in both steels.

unreadable_items: panel (c): SAED inset index labels partly illegible at the supplied resolution (only some (hkl)ε and zone-axis labels can be read)
panels (b), (e), (f): small SAED index and zone-axis text is faint; Miller indices are transcribed only where legible
no axis scales or numeric data are printed on any micrograph, so carbide dimensions quoted in the citing text cannot be verified from the pixels
